reference.source: Primer on the Metabolic Bone Diseases / Williams Textbook of Endocrinology
clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive phosphate-wasting rickets caused by loss-of-function mutations in SLC34A3, encoding the renal sodium-phosphate cotransporter NaPi-IIc
Unlike FGF23-driven disorders, phosphate wasting here is FGF23-independent and provokes an appropriate, brisk rise in 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D
The high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D increases intestinal calcium absorption, causing suppressed parathyroid hormone and the defining hypercalciuria
Presents with rickets, bone pain, short stature, and often renal complications such as nephrolithiasis or nephrocalcinosis from the hypercalciuria
The biochemical signature is hypophosphataemia with renal phosphate wasting, HIGH 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, low-normal parathyroid hormone, and hypercalciuria
This pattern is the mirror image of FGF23-mediated rickets, where 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D is inappropriately low
Treatment is oral phosphate replacement ALONE; adding active vitamin D is contraindicated because it would worsen the already high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D and aggravate hypercalciuria and stones
reference.pathophysiology: SLC34A3 encodes NaPi-IIc, a proximal tubule sodium-phosphate cotransporter that reclaims filtered phosphate. Biallelic loss-of-function mutations cause primary renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphataemia. Crucially, this occurs without elevated FGF23, so the normal compensatory response is intact: hypophosphataemia stimulates 1-alpha-hydroxylase and raises 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D. The elevated active hormone increases intestinal calcium absorption, suppressing parathyroid hormone and delivering a calcium load that the kidney excretes as hypercalciuria, predisposing to nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis. Chronic hypophosphataemia impairs mineralisation, producing rickets and osteomalacia. The therapeutic implication is decisive: phosphate is replaced but active vitamin D is avoided, since it would exacerbate hypercalciuria.
additionalDifferentials: X-linked and other FGF23-mediated hypophosphataemic rickets
Autosomal dominant and recessive hypophosphataemic rickets
Fanconi syndrome with generalised proximal tubulopathy
Dent disease and other hereditary renal phosphate-wasting tubulopathies
additionalInvestigations: Serum phosphate with tubular reabsorption of phosphate confirming renal wasting
1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D, characteristically HIGH, distinguishing HHRH from FGF23-driven disease
Renal ultrasound for nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
SLC34A3 gene sequencing to confirm NaPi-IIc deficiency
redFlags: Recurrent renal stones or progressive nephrocalcinosis
Declining renal function from chronic calcium deposition
Severe skeletal deformity or growth failure
Worsening hypercalciuria if active vitamin D is inappropriately added
reference.prognosis: With phosphate replacement alone, rickets and growth typically improve while hypercalciuria abates as phosphate normalises; long-term renal prognosis depends on the burden of nephrocalcinosis and stones accrued before diagnosis and correct management.
pitfalls: Treating like FGF23-driven rickets and adding active vitamin D, which aggravates hypercalciuria and stone formation
Missing the high 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D that defines the disorder and reverses the usual treatment logic
Overlooking hypercalciuria and its renal consequences
Failing to sequence SLC34A3 and mislabelling the phosphate-wasting mechanism
references: Primer on the Metabolic Bone Diseases and Disorders of Mineral Metabolism
management: Phosphate replacement alone, given orally in divided doses, is the definitive treatment and restores mineralisation, healing rickets and osteomalacia
Avoid active vitamin D analogues, which are unnecessary and worsen the hypercalciuria that defines this disorder, in contrast to FGF23-mediated rickets
Maintain good hydration and monitor urinary calcium to reduce the risk of nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis
Renal tract ultrasound surveillance for nephrocalcinosis and calculi to protect long-term renal function
Track serum phosphate, calcium, parathyroid hormone, alkaline phosphatase, linear growth and radiographic bone healing on treatment
Coordinated metabolic bone and nephrology follow-up
Genetic counselling and cascade family testing for SLC34A3 (NaPi-IIc) variants
